subject.title: fix: use platform percentiles for temporal abuse signals

question: Should the temporal benchmark use a resumable full-population scan, or may it intentionally stop producing percentile signals when the active-skill population or runtime exceeds the 8,000-skill bound?
rationale: The branch establishes a permanent operational failure mode whose acceptability depends on moderation coverage and cron-capacity intent, which tests alone cannot determine.

options.title: Make the scan resumable
options.body: Continue bounded scan pages across invocations and publish only after a complete active-population snapshot, preserving full-platform semantics as the corpus grows.

options.title: Accept a guarded ceiling
options.body: Keep the 8,000-skill fail-closed bound but add explicit monitoring, operator recovery documentation, and evidence that current production scale has sufficient headroom.

options.title: Retain the current cohort
options.body: Keep the existing bounded cohort behavior until a scalable full-population implementation and runtime proof are available.

recommendation.title: Make the scan resumable
recommendation.body: Continue bounded scan pages across invocations and publish only after a complete active-population snapshot, preserving full-platform semantics as the corpus grows.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and merged the temporal scan and are the strongest history-based owner for its completion and persistence contract.
